title: PACE-HNC Study: Postoperative Ambulation and Clinical Evaluation After Major Head and Neck Cancer Surgery
summary:
Patients undergoing major surgery for head and neck cancer often experience reduced physical mobility during the first days after surgery. Early mobilization, including sitting, standing, and walking, is an important part of postoperative recovery. However, mobility is usually assessed through observations and documentation by healthcare professionals, which may not fully reflect how much patients actually move.

The PACE-HNC study aims to better understand physical activity and mobility during the early recovery period after major head and neck cancer surgery.

A total of 60 adult patients will be included in this study. Following surgery, participants will wear a small activity monitor (ActiGraph) on their wrist during their hospital stay. The device records body movements and allows researchers to measure physical activity and periods of inactivity. Monitoring will continue until approximately the fourth or fifth day after surgery or until hospital discharge, whichever occurs first.

In addition, healthcare professionals will assess patients' mobility once daily using a standardized clinical scale. Information about the surgery, postoperative pain, complications, and length of hospital stay will also be collected. Physical function will be assessed before surgery and at the end of the observation period using handgrip strength measurements and questionnaires. Participants will also be asked about their experience wearing the activity monitor.

The study is purely observational. No experimental treatments or additional medications will be administered, and routine medical care and postoperative mobilization will not be changed.

The findings may help improve our understanding of recovery after major head and neck cancer surgery and support the development of future postoperative mobilization and rehabilitation programs.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx
Malignant neoplasm of nasal cavity and middle ear

interventions.name:
Single observational cohort: Adult patients undergoing major surgical resection for head and neck cancer with a planned postoperative inpatient stay.

Objective postoperative mobility will be continuously monitored using a wrist-worn ActiGraph wGT3X-BT accelerometer from POD 0 or POD 1 until POD 4

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥18 years.
2. Undergoing major surgical resection for head and neck cancer requiring postoperative inpatient admission, including procedures with or without neck dissection and/or microvascular free-flap reconstruction.
3. Ability to provide informed consent preoperatively.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Planned postoperative hospital admission of less than 24 hours.
2. Preoperative inability to ambulate independently or with assistance.
3. Severe cognitive impairment or inability to comply with study procedures.
4. Contraindications to wearing a wearable device (e.g., relevant skin conditions).
